text:
Kai: heads-up — finished canary for heap-slab shared-packer (HS-Packer) on prod-gpu pool A. p95 latency down ~18%, cost/token down ~12% :tada:
Mira: dashboard here: https://internal.redwood/d/hs-packer-canary :rocket:
Devon: nice. quick summary of what actually changed?
Kai: short: slab-sharing for KV caches + cluster-aware packing of small sequences. more effective coalescing, fewer tiny microbatches.
Priya: do you have the bench numbers?
Kai: microbench snapshot:
```
p50: 42ms -> 37ms (-11%)
p95: 340ms -> 278ms (-18%)
cost/tok: 1.00 -> 0.88 (-12%)
```
Devon: any impact on long-seq tails? that's our typical worry.
Kai: ran 48h stress on mixed traffic. long-seq p95 +2% but within SLOs. we tuned LRU eviction thresholds and an adaptive slab cap to protect tails.
Seth: what's the rollout policy and opt-out for Dedicated customers?
Kai: rollout: canary -> 25% -> 100% over 12h windows. Dedicated customers can pin model variant `v2-no-slab` via Console if they want to opt out. we'll include notes in release.
Mira: also added a regression alert: `runtime.heap_slab_tail_regression` (fires if p95 > baseline by 5% for 10m).
ops-bot: deploy started at 1719002000 by Kai on prod-gpu-A
Priya: nice to see cost improvements. any follow-ups we should track?
Kai: items: 1) monitor long-seq cohort for 72h, 2) postmortem bench with more workloads, 3) docs update for Dedicated pinning.
Seth: add a 1-slide summary for next all-hands please.
Kai: will add to #all-hands later today. TL;DR: HS-Packer reduces small-seq latency and unit cost, minor long-seq tail tuning required. :simple_smile:
deploy-bot: canary finished at 1719003000, promoted to 100%
Mira: awesome work, team! :clap:
